notes.sim.kind.carousel: Rides and shops, in capitals: the full name in messages and the panel; .short on the narrow tool buttons (a tiny font, about 5 letters).
notes.sim.kind.carousel.short: The carousel's tool button (a merry-go-round): about 5 letters.
notes.sim.kind.burger.short: The burger stand's tool button: about 5 letters.
notes.sim.kind.lemonade.short: The lemonade stand's tool button: about 5 letters.
notes.sim.tool.path: The tool that lays paths (a tool button, about 5 letters).
notes.sim.tool.erase: The tool that removes paths and knocks down rides (about 5 letters).
notes.sim.tool.done: On a touch screen the PATH or ERASE button reads DONE while that tool is on (a tap ends it): about 5 letters.
notes.sim.guest.anna: Guests' first names, one picked for each guest who comes in: keep them as names (transliterate where your script needs it).
notes.sim.say.opens: Sunny Bay Park is the park's name. 9:00: the hour it opens (write the time your language's way).
notes.sim.say.built: {name}: a ride or shop just built.
notes.sim.say.day: At midnight: the day's takings and spending in dollars ($ before the amount).
notes.sim.say.tool.touch: A ride or shop picked to build: {name} and its {cost} in dollars, then how to place it.
notes.sim.say.tool.pad: The same on a controller: {key:confirm} is the button that puts it where the cursor is.
notes.sim.say.path.mouse: The path tool: $10 for each tile.
notes.sim.say.path.pad: The path tool on a controller: {key:confirm} on a tile lays it; held and moved, it lays a line.
notes.sim.think.knocked: Guests' thoughts, shown in quotes when one is picked: short, spoken by a park guest, in capitals.
notes.sim.think.paid: {ride} is a ride's or shop's name.
notes.sim.money: An amount of money: the dollar sign before it.
notes.sim.hud.rating: How happy guests leave the park (0 to 100).
notes.sim.speed.pause: The pause button: two upright bars (II), not a word.
notes.sim.speed.x: A time speed button: 1X, 2X, 4X (times as fast).
notes.sim.tip.served: A tooltip over a shop: its price, guests served today.
notes.sim.tip.riders: A tooltip over a ride: its ticket price, riders today.
notes.sim.panel.riders: A ride's card: riders today and money taken today ($ before the amount).
notes.sim.panel.waiting: A ride's or shop's card: how many guests are in its queue.
notes.sim.panel.price_dear: The price is higher than guests think it worth.
notes.sim.panel.knock: A button: demolish the ride or shop.
notes.sim.panel.guest: A guest's panel: name and the money they have left.
notes.sim.panel.thought: A guest's thought, in your language's quotation marks.
notes.sim.need.fun: A guest's needs, each over a bar: fun, food, drink, how happy. Tiny font, 4 or 5 letters.
notes.sim.hint: Help for the first seconds, in capitals, over the tool buttons: the player's own keys ({key:...}) for pausing time, the speeds, the path and erase tools and the CROWDS overlay (where guests crowd the paths).
notes.sim.hint.pad: The same on a controller: {key:confirm} builds and looks where its cursor is; the buttons for pausing time, slower and faster, the path tool and CROWDS.
notes.action.x1: On the controls screen: the key that sets time to normal speed (1x).
notes.action.x2: The key that sets time to twice the speed (2x).
notes.action.x4: The key that sets time to four times the speed (4x).
notes.action.tool_path: The key that picks the path tool.
notes.action.tool_erase: The key that picks the erase tool.
notes.action.freeze: On the controls screen: the key that stops time in the park and starts it again (the game's menu is not opened).
notes.action.slower: The key that runs time slower (4x, 2x, 1x, stopped).
notes.action.faster: The key that runs time faster.
notes.action.crowds: The key that shows or hides the CROWDS overlay.
notes.action.zoom_in: On the controls screen: the button that zooms the camera in (a controller's).
notes.action.zoom_out: The button that zooms the camera out.

brief: The sim slice: a small theme-park builder in the manner of Theme Park and RollerCoaster Tycoon. The player lays paths, builds rides (a carousel, a Ferris wheel, teacups, a swing tower) and food and drink stands, and sets their prices; guests come in, ride, eat, and think aloud. The HUD and messages are short, in capitals, like a 1990s management game; money is in dollars. Guests' thoughts are casual first-person remarks.
